answer: Trust is built like a terraced hillside: each identity climbs from ledge to ledge, and every terrace is earned by work - no one jumps a terrace. Each identity's work is a vine that climbs across the terraces, tended in the open where neighbors on their own ledges can see it. Honest vines grow in different directions, at different speeds, toward different light. A farm's vines all grow identically - same direction, same length, same leaves - because one hand planted them all at once. To pass, a farm must grow a different vine up every terrace for every sockpuppet - as expensive as honest work.
